newsitem.title: UK: UK Treasury says "natural" unemployment 5% to 7%.
newsitem.headline: UK Treasury says "natural" unemployment 5% to 7%.

text.p: The UK Treasury's chief economic adviser, Alan Budd, said the "natural" rate of unemployment consistent with stable inflation was probably between five and seven percent.
Budd told parliament's Treasury Select Committee there was a range of uncertainty about the size of the ouput gap of zero to three percent.

"There would be an equivalent range of uncertainty about the rate of unemployment which is consistent with stable inflation, and I suppose that range would be somewhere in the range of five to seven percent unemployment," he said.
Unemployment was 7.2 percent of the workforce in October, a five-year low.
Budd added that giving a range implied "a degree of knowledge that we simply do not possess."
If inflation did not accelerate, this would suggest "that our policies have been successful in bringing this natural rate, as I'll call it, down."
Budd said the behaviour of earnings encouraged the Treasury to believe "that we are not yet down to the natural rate of unemployment."
